scope: v2: recommendation consistency + tone + sample-vs-total + hedged-vs-asserted

findings.message: The 'About This Report' section mixes first-person voice ('We audited', 'We fetch', 'We then review') with the 'Discovery Files / llms.txt' sub-section which switches to third-person impersonal ('We found no llms.txt', but then 'We recommend' — consistent), however the llms-full.txt sub-section uses a hedged third-person construction ('Whether adding it would be worthwhile depends on the depth of content across the full 107-page set, which our sample of 12 pages does not yet measure; we recommend revisiting') while every other Priority and Finding section uses direct first-person assertions — this is minor and arguably consistent. Re-examining: the material inconsistency is in the Findings body: Priority 1 through Priority 3 and all narrative sections use first-person ('We score', 'We recommend', 'We cannot confirm'), but the 'Structured Data Findings' section abruptly shifts to third-person passive ('The audit found no gaps'), breaking the consistent first-person voice held throughout all other Finding sections.
findings.context: The audit found no gaps in the Schema.org property coverage on the audited pages.

findings.message: The Discovery Files / llms.txt section states 'We found no llms.txt at mx.allabout.network' as a site-wide assertion, but contradicts the Findings Priority 1 and the Cross-Page Consistency table (which shows 'llms.txt link tag: 100%' across all audited pages), implying llms.txt is present — this is a data conflict, not a scope issue. The material sample-vs-total overreach is in the Executive Summary, which states 'mx.allabout.network has already reached a position where machines can discover, parse, and act on the content with commercial confidence' and 'the MX governance markers are present across the audited pages' — these are appropriately scoped. The clearest overreach is in the Balanced Scorecard Machine Experience section, which asserts 'machines can discover, parse, cite, and transact with confidence' without any sample-scope qualifier, implying this holds for the full site when only 12 of 107 pages were audited.
findings.context: Across the audited set of 12 pages, machines can discover, parse, cite, and transact with confidence

findings.message: The Discovery Files llms.txt section asserts 'We found no llms.txt at mx.allabout.network' as a site-wide absence, but the Cross-Page Consistency table records 'llms.txt link tag: 100%' across all 12 audited pages, and Priority 1 in Findings states that llms.txt is present — the only gap is llms-full.txt. The llms.txt absence claim is an overreaching site-wide assertion that contradicts the sample evidence.
findings.context: We found no llms.txt at mx.allabout.network, meaning machines that query the host for a structured content index receive no site description
